- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 5–15% for the next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 10–20% for the next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >20% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.2x the prior peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 2.00), model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 10–15% for next 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 10–20% downward bias for days 1–7, then adjust to historical mean reversion after day 8.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1.00, 0.00, 1.00), model tends to misalign with sentiment; align forecast to sentiment’s last 3-day average for next 5 days.
